name: Rosewood Villa Magna
positioning: City hotel on Madrid's Paseo de la Castellana with Northern Spanish cooking at Amós and rooftop Houses with views of Madrid
best_for: Travelers who want a Paseo de la Castellana base within strolling distance of major art museums
Families or friends who want combinable suites with two to four bedrooms
Food lovers interested in Cantabrian cooking and a chef-led market walk

facts.text: The hotel is on Madrid's Paseo de la Castellana.
The hotel is within strolling distance of major art museums and within a block of a Metro station.
Amós Restaurant is led by Executive Chef Jesús Sánchez and draws on the cuisine of Cantabria and Northern Spain.
Las Brasas de Castellana serves traditional Spanish cuisine around a grill, with an open kitchen and a garden terrace.
Breakfast at Las Brasas de Castellana ranges from a continental spread to à la carte dishes prepared on the grill.
Tarde.O Bar combines a bar with a modern terrace and serves handcrafted cocktails and gourmet bites.
Flor y Nata Patisserie is an all-day cafe for morning coffees, light lunches and afternoon get-togethers.
Sunday Brunch is held at Las Brasas de Castellana with a live band.
Rooms have garden or boulevard views.
The hotel offers a private tour and picnic at El Escorial.

highlights.text: The Signature Suites are Houses located on the hotel's rooftop with views of Madrid.
Amós serves local delicacies such as Cantabrian anchovies, Riofrío caviar and organic wines.
Combinable suites and houses offer two to four bedrooms and a separate living area.
Guests can join the Executive Chef on a guided tour of local markets.

considerations.text: The Royal Palace and Gran Vía are a long walk from the hotel, but taxis are plentiful.
WhataHotel notes limited recreational facilities compared with resort properties.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Rosewood Villa Magna review
